sections.h2: What is included in a hedge trim
paras: Every job starts with a look at the hedge and a chat about what you want. Some people want a sharp formal box or murraya line along a path. Others want a loose, natural shape on a photinia screen so it stops leaning over the fence. The hedge trimming Canberra customers ask us for is rarely the same twice, so we work to the look you want.
Height reduction is common on older lilly pilly and conifer hedges that have crept up and now block light or views. We bring the height down in stages where the plant needs it, so it recovers evenly.

sections.h2: Timing hedge cuts around Canberra's frosts
paras: Canberra's hard frosts run from about May to August, and a hedge cut hard just before them can suffer. Fresh cuts expose soft growth, frost burns it, and you are left with brown tips until spring. For most species we avoid heavy reductions from late autumn through winter and keep those months to light tidying.

Spring is when growth takes off, so a shape in early spring and a second trim in late summer keeps most hedges tight for the year. Conifers are less forgiving, so we never cut them back into old brown wood, because it will not reshoot. Good hedge trimming Canberra wide follows the frost calendar more than the date on the wall.

faqs.q: How much does hedge trimming Canberra wide cost?
faqs.a: Every quote is free and given upfront. The price depends on the length and height of the hedge, the species, how overgrown it is and how much waste there is to remove. Send a photo with your suburb and rough measurements and we will give you a figure before any work starts.

faqs.q: Do you take the hedge clippings away after trimming in Woden Valley?
faqs.a: Yes. Green waste is removed after every hedge trimming Canberra job, in Woden Valley, Weston Creek and the Inner South alike. We rake, blow and load the clippings and take them with us, so nothing is left at the kerb or stuffed into your green bin. Removal is part of the quote, not an extra.

faqs.q: Can you reduce the height of an overgrown hedge?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Photinia, lilly pilly, pittosporum and murraya can be brought down hard and will reshoot. Conifers will not regrow from old brown wood, so we reduce them only as far as there is green growth. We will tell you what is safe before we start.

faqs.q: Should I choose a formal or an informal hedge?
faqs.a: A formal hedge has flat faces, a level top and crisp corners, and suits box, murraya and pittosporum because they fill in quickly. An informal hedge is rounded and looser, which suits photinia and larger screens where privacy matters more than precision. For hedge trimming Canberra homeowners often want a mix of both.

faqs.q: Do you trim hedges as part of regular garden maintenance?
faqs.a: Yes. Many customers add a trim to a scheduled garden maintenance visit two or three times a year, so the hedge never gets away from them. Others book hedge trimming Canberra jobs as one-offs before a sale or an event. Either way, the clippings leave with us.
